'''''Euphorbia pedroi''''' (known in [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]] as '''''eufórbia-de-gomes-pedro''''' or '''''tabaíba-do-espichel''''') is a species of flowering plant in the [[Euphorbiaceae|spurge family]] [[endemic]] to the [[Arrábida Natural Park]] in [[Portugal]]. It is part of section Aphyllis, a mostly African and [[Macaronesia]]n clade, being the only member of its section native to Europe.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Barres |first1=Laia |last2=Vilatersana |first2=Roser |last3=Molero |first3=Julià |last4=Susanna |first4=Alfonso |last5=Galbany-Casals |first5=Mercè |title=Molecular phylogeny of Euphorbia subg. Esula sect. Aphyllis (Euphorbiaceae) inferred from nrDNA and cpDNA markers with biogeographic insights |journal=Taxon |date=June 2011 |volume=60 |issue=3 |pages=705–720 |doi=10.1002/tax.603007 |hdl=10261/38986 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221672463 |access-date=10 January 2023|hdl-access=free }}</ref> Its binomial name is dedicated to José Gomes Pedro (1915–2010), a [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] botanist who studied the flora and vegetation of Arrábida and Mozambique.<ref name="flora-on" />

==Description==
''Euphorbia pedroi'' is a sub-succulent shrub that can reach {{convert|2|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> Leaves are {{convert|25|-|60|x|4|-|10|mm|in|abbr=on}}, green or somewhat [[glaucous]]. [[Cyathium]] is {{convert|2.8|-|4|mm|in|abbr=on}} with a {{convert|1|-|3|mm|in|abbr=on}} [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]], glabrous or slightly hairy both in the base and peduncle. Fruit is {{convert|4.2|-|5|x|5.8|-|7.2|mm|in|abbr=on}} yellowish-green or reddish, seeds are reddish brown, {{convert|2.8|-|3.2|x|2|-|2.3|mm|in|abbr=on}} and somewhat dorsiventrally flattened.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=E. pedroi |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/08_108_06%20Euphorbia.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=13 December 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Euphorbia pedroi'' is native to the [[Arrábida Natural Park]], specifically between [[Cabo Espichel]] and [[Sesimbra]] on the [[Setúbal Peninsula]], in the [[Atlantic]] coast. It is found on slopes of south-facing [[limestone]] cliffs on incipient soils or rock cracks subjected to regular mist and strong winds.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /><ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Euphorbia pedroi Molero & Rovira |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Euphorbia+pedroi |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=13 December 2020}}</ref>
